story.title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed for First Time Due to Severe Weather
story.summary: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed for the first time in its history, now scheduled to take place on Saturday. The decision was made due to forecasts of severe weather, including high winds, expected to impact New York City during the event.

explore_lenses.label: Why is postponing the parade significant?
explore_lenses.title: A break with a century-old schedule
explore_lenses.summary: The move interrupts a Thanksgiving-morning tradition during the parade's 100th annual edition, rather than merely changing the handling of its balloons. The parade has been suspended before, during World War II, but reporting describes this as its first weather postponement.

claims.text: Macy's said the event, originally set for Thursday, November 26, will instead begin at 8:30 a.m. Saturday, November 28.
CBS reported that the parade was suspended from 1942 through 1944 during World War II, but had not previously been postponed because of weather.
The city had planned for more than 3.5 million spectators along the route, illustrating the scale of public-safety and transportation disruption involved in changing the date.

explore_lenses.label: Why was a postponement chosen over limits?
explore_lenses.title: The forecast posed broader safety risks
explore_lenses.summary: The decision followed Macy's consultation with city and agency partners as a coastal storm threatened rain, damaging winds and coastal flooding. Wind risk matters particularly for the parade's giant balloons, but the cited forecasts also pointed to hazards for spectators and operations more generally.

claims.text: Macy's said participant and spectator safety was its priority and that it made the change after consulting city and agency partners.

Forecast: In its November 25 afternoon discussion, the National Weather Service said the Thanksgiving storm would bring rain and strong to damaging winds, with widespread moderate coastal flooding likely around high tides.
Forecast: The same NWS discussion said the timing of the heaviest rain and wind still had model uncertainty, though impacts were most likely Thursday afternoon and evening.

ABC News reported that parade rules bar giant balloons from flying when sustained winds exceed 23 mph or gusts exceed 34 mph, and that the NYPD makes the final decision based on conditions along the route.

story_report.summary: Macy’s has postponed its Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday because of an expected severe-weather system, shifting an event that had been scheduled for Thursday, Nov. 26. The parade is now set to begin at 8:30 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 28, in what Macy’s and news reports described as the first weather-related postponement in the event’s history. Macy’s said safety for participants and spectators drove the decision after consultation with city and agency partners.

sections.heading: Parade Weather Postponement History
sections.body: The parade was suspended from 1942 through 1944 during World War II, according to CBS, but it had not previously been postponed because of weather. The forecast that prompted the change called for rain, strong to damaging winds and likely widespread moderate coastal flooding around high tides. The National Weather Service said the most consequential rain and wind impacts were most likely Thursday afternoon and evening, although the precise timing remained uncertain.

sections.heading: Safety Rules and Event Disruption
sections.body: Macy’s said it prioritized participant and spectator safety in changing the schedule. The decision affects an event for which the city had planned for more than 3.5 million route spectators, while marching bands and other performers who had planned for Thursday must make alternative arrangements. Parade rules bar giant balloons when sustained winds exceed 23 mph or gusts exceed 34 mph; the NYPD makes the final call based on conditions along the route.

sections.heading: Saturday Parade Logistics Remain Pending
sections.body: Macy’s said its team was working through the operational logistics of moving the parade and would release further details once they are finalized. A pre-postponement city notice listed Thursday street closures, not revised Saturday guidance. The earlier National Weather Service outlook also said Saturday could bring lower flight conditions and west wind gusts of 20 to 30 knots in the New York metro area.

unresolved.text: Macy’s had not publicly finalized revised route operations, the participant lineup, spectator-access plans or other logistical details for Saturday.
Forecast wind speeds along the parade route, whether balloon restrictions would be triggered, and Saturday’s final weather conditions remained uncertain when the postponement was announced.

related_stories.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia Arrives in Spain After Leaving the U.S.
related_stories.summary: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, an El Salvador native who was mistakenly deported by ICE last year, has left the United States and arrived in Spain. His departure marks the conclusion of a 20-month legal battle related to his deportation, which became emblematic of the Trump administration's immigration policies. Garcia traveled to Spain with his wife, stating he feels like a 'free man' after the ordeal.

related_stories.title: Thousands Protest in Athens Over Rising Living Costs
related_stories.summary: On November 25, 2026, approximately 14,000 people marched in Athens as part of a 24-hour strike against rising living costs and stagnant wages. The industrial action led to significant disruptions, including halted metro services, grounded flights, and ferries remaining in port.

related_stories.title: Russian Strikes Kill Seven in Ukraine; Kyiv Targets Refineries
related_stories.summary: Russian drone attacks resulted in the deaths of seven people across six Ukrainian regions, targeting infrastructure including a gas production facility and a thermal power plant. In response, Ukraine launched drone strikes on Russian oil refineries in the Samara and Rostov regions, as well as an airbase in Nizhny Novgorod, leading to at least one reported death in the Samara region.
